mcqs.question: The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026, were notified by which authority and on what date?
mcqs.explanation: The Legal Metrology (Indian Standard Time) Rules, 2026, were notified by the Union government on August 27, 2026. The most tempting wrong option is August 28, but the notification date was August 27, 2026.

mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The IST® trademark was registered by CSIR-NPL in 2024.
Reason (R): The IST® trademark was registered by CSIR-NPL in 2025.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Assertion A is true because CSIR-NPL registered the IST® trademark in 2024. Reason R is false because the registration year was 2024, not 2025.

mcqs.question: How many Regional Reference Standard Laboratories maintain secondary time scales for Indian Standard Time?
mcqs.explanation: Five Regional Reference Standard Laboratories maintain secondary time scales for IST. The nearby figures three, four and six are incorrect.

mcqs.question: Where was the White Rabbit-based IST dissemination network commissioned in July 2026?
mcqs.explanation: The White Rabbit-based IST dissemination network was commissioned at RRSL Bengaluru in July 2026. Hyderabad, Mumbai and New Delhi were not the stated commissioning location.

mcqs.question:
Match the time-dissemination technologies with their stated accuracy levels:

List-I
(a) NTP
(b) PTP
(c) Satellite links
(d) Optical links

List-II
(i) Nanoseconds
(ii) Picoseconds
(iii) Milliseconds
(iv) Microseconds
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are NTP–milliseconds, PTP–microseconds, satellite links–nanoseconds and optical links–picoseconds: a-iii, b-iv, c-i, d-ii. The other codes interchange the accuracy levels assigned to these technologies.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly describes NavIC, earlier known as IRNSS?
options: It was developed after GPS data was denied during the Kargil War and carries atomic clocks.
It was developed after GPS data was denied during the Kargil War and carries mechanical clocks.
It was developed before the Kargil War and carries atomic clocks.
It was developed after GPS data was denied during the Kargil War and carries optical clocks.
mcqs.explanation: NavIC, earlier IRNSS, was developed after GPS data was denied during the Kargil War and carries atomic clocks. The alternatives alter either the development context or the type of clocks carried.

mcqs.question: Which statement accurately reflects the status of State-level Uniform Civil Code measures mentioned in the September 2026 debate?
options: Uttarakhand has had the UCC in force since January 2025, while the Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh Bills await Presidential assent.
Uttarakhand has had the UCC in force since January 2024, while the Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh Bills await Presidential assent.
Uttarakhand has had the UCC in force since January 2025, while the Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh Bills have received Presidential assent.
Uttarakhand has had the UCC in force since January 2025, while the Assam, Gujarat and Rajasthan Bills await Presidential assent.
mcqs.explanation: Uttarakhand’s UCC has been in force since January 2025, whereas the UCC Bills of Assam, Gujarat and Madhya Pradesh await Presidential assent. The other options change the year, the assent status or one of the States.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: State-level Uniform Civil Codes exempt tribal populations.
Statement B: State-level Uniform Civil Codes exempt coastal populations.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Statement A is true because State UCCs exempt tribal populations. Statement B is false because the stated exemption is for tribal populations, not coastal populations.

mcqs.question: What was the principal reform focus of the Law Commission’s 2018 consultation paper in the UCC debate?
options: Replacing all State laws with a single tax code
Creating a separate criminal code for tribal populations
mcqs.explanation: The Law Commission’s 2018 consultation paper focused on reforming discriminatory personal laws. The other options describe subjects not identified as the paper’s reform focus.

mcqs.question:
Match the case with the legal point associated with it:

List-I
(a) Shah Bano
(b) Sarla Mudgal
(c) Daniel Latifi
(d) John Vallamattom

List-II
(i) Conversion for second marriage invalid
(ii) Struck down Section 118 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925
(iii) Maintenance under Section 125 CrPC
(iv) Upheld the Muslim Women Act, 1986
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Shah Bano–maintenance under Section 125 CrPC, Sarla Mudgal–conversion for second marriage invalid, Daniel Latifi–upheld the Muslim Women Act, 1986, and John Vallamattom–struck Section 118 of the Indian Succession Act, 1925. The other codes mismatch these case holdings.

mcqs.question:
Match each case with the associated legal point:

List-I
(a) Shayara Bano
(b) Jose Paulo Coutinho
(c) Section 6A Citizenship Act case, 2024

List-II
(i) Goa as an example of a common civil code
(ii) Instant triple talaq invalid
(iii) Casteism and gender discrimination cannot claim Article 29 protection
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Shayara Bano–instant triple talaq invalid, Jose Paulo Coutinho–Goa as an example of a common civil code, and the Section 6A Citizenship Act case–casteism and gender discrimination cannot claim Article 29 protection. The other options interchange these three legal points.
